title: FBISE Section A Board Examination Simulator 08 (Full-Book Board Simulator I)
subject: english-10

questions.question: She said, "Alas! I have lost my purse." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She exclaimed with joy that she lost her purse.
options.B: She exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her purse.
options.C: She told with sorrow that she has lost her purse.
options.D: She cried that her purse had lost.

questions.explanation: Interjection 'Alas!' indicates grief, converting the reporting verb to 'exclaimed with sorrow', followed by tense backshift from present perfect to past perfect ('had lost').

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'She can solve this mathematical problem.'

options.A: This mathematical problem can be solved by her.
options.B: This mathematical problem could be solved by her.
options.C: This mathematical problem can solve by her.
options.D: This mathematical problem is solved by her.

questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary 'can' takes 'can be + past participle' ('can be solved') in passive voice; the tense of the modal does not change.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The jury ___ unanimous in its decision.'
questions.explanation: When a collective noun ('jury') acts as a single, undivided unit (signaled by 'unanimous' and 'its'), it takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Identify the underlined verbal: 'The *sunken* ship was discovered by deep-sea divers.'
questions.explanation: 'Sunken' is an archaic/attributive past participle form of 'sink' modifying the noun 'ship'.

questions.question: Identify the underlined part: 'The boy *with blue eyes* is my cousin.'
questions.explanation: 'with blue eyes' is a prepositional phrase modifying the noun 'The boy', functioning adjectivally as an Adjective Phrase.

questions.question: Choose the correct modal for formal permission: '___ I come in, sir?'
questions.explanation: 'May' is the formal and grammatically respectful modal auxiliary for requesting permission from an authority figure.

questions.question: Identify the type of pronoun: 'The boy *whose* bicycle was stolen lodged a complaint.'
questions.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession and connects the subordinate clause to the antecedent noun 'The boy', qualifying as a Possessive Relative Pronoun.

questions.question: Choose the correct correlative pair: 'Neither the teacher ___ the principal attended the meeting.'
questions.explanation: 'Neither' strictly pairs with 'nor' as correlative conjunctions.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'He congratulated his friend ___ securing the top position.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'congratulate' takes the dependent preposition 'on' (or 'upon'), not 'for'.

questions.question: Identify the sound device in: 'Men sell the wedding bells.'
questions.explanation: The repetition of the short vowel sound /ɛ/ across 'men', 'sell', 'wedding', and 'bells' is Assonance.

questions.question: He said, "How beautiful the rainbow is!" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He exclaimed that the rainbow was very beautiful.
options.B: He said that how beautiful was the rainbow.
options.C: He asked how beautiful the rainbow is.
options.D: He exclaimed with wonder that the rainbow is very beautiful.

questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences beginning with 'How/What' expressing admiration change into assertive clauses with intensifiers like 'very beautiful' and past tense 'was'.

questions.question: Which of the following verbs CANNOT be converted into passive voice?
questions.explanation: 'Sleep' is an intransitive verb; intransitive verbs cannot take a direct object and therefore cannot be converted into the passive voice.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The jury ___ divided in their opinions.'
questions.explanation: When members of a collective noun act individually in disagreement (indicated by 'divided' and 'their'), it takes a plural verb ('were').

questions.question: Identify the underlined clause: 'He was so weak *that he could barely stand*.'
questions.explanation: 'that he could barely stand' connected to the intensifier 'so weak' denotes the outcome/result of his weakness, making it an Adverb Clause of Result.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be postponed.'
questions.explanation: In a First Conditional, future time in the conditional clause is expressed using the simple present tense ('rains'), never 'will rain'.
